exact_cwe_mechanism.evidence: CWE-918 requires a server-side component making requests to unexpected destinations. This is client-side JavaScript executing in the browser, making requests from the user's browser to external domains, not server-side request forgery.

connection.evidence: data-youtube attribute value from DOM (user-controlled) directly interpolated into img.src URL without validation, creating a direct connection from user input to resource loading.

diff_causality.evidence: If this line were removed, the img element would have no src attribute and would not load any image. The line creates the resource loading behavior.

security_control.evidence: No validation of the id parameter before URL construction. The only check is existence of the attribute.
security_control.required_control: Input validation/sanitization to ensure id parameter contains only valid YouTube video ID characters
security_control.control_requirement_evidence: For safe URL construction, the id should be validated to prevent injection of unexpected characters or domains
existing_controls_checked: Only checks if youtube attribute exists and elem is not null (line 92)
security_control.deficiency_evidence: No validation of the id value itself; it's directly interpolated into the URL template without sanitization

concrete_impact.evidence: Potential for loading images from unexpected sources if id parameter contains unexpected characters that modify the URL domain or path, but limited to img.youtube.com domain constraint.

diff_counterfactual: If the candidate line were reverted, the img element would be created but would have no src attribute, preventing any image loading from YouTube or any other domain.
supporting_evidence: data-youtube attribute value from DOM is directly used in URL construction without validation
img.src assignment loads external resource from constructed URL
The line creates the resource loading behavior that would not exist without it
contradicting_evidence: CWE-918 specifically requires server-side request forgery; this is client-side JavaScript executing in user's browser
The request originates from user's browser to img.youtube.com, not from a server to unexpected destinations
The domain is hardcoded as img.youtube.com, limiting potential for requests to arbitrary servers
unresolved_facts: Whether data-youtube values are validated/sanitized before being set in HTML
Whether YouTube's img.youtube.com service validates video IDs before serving images
Whether id parameter can contain characters that would redirect to different domains
